slides.title: Fernwood
slides.subtitle: Heritage homes, a village square, and a church that took up theatre

slides.title: Fernwood Manor
slides.body: In 1860, surveyor Benjamin Pearse built a stone villa here and called it Fernwood Manor. The house came down in 1969. The name refused to leave.

slides.title: Spring Ridge
slides.body: Freshwater springs along a gravel ridge here were an important source of Victoria's drinking water until the mid-1870s. Hydrating Victoria before it was cool.

slides.title: Fernwood Square
slides.body: At Gladstone and Fernwood. The end of the Spring Ridge streetcar line from 1891 to 1948, and a public square since the 1970s. People still end up here.

slides.title: From pews to plays
slides.body: The Belfry Theatre has been in this former Baptist church since 1976. Main building: 1892. Still the most dramatic building in the neighbourhood.

slides.title: Old streets, old houses
slides.body: Many of Fernwood's streets and houses date from 1890 to 1912, and the village is a heritage conservation area. The 1890s ones have now seen three centuries.

slides.title: Vic High & green space
slides.body: Victoria High School's building went up in 1911–14. Alexander Park and Stadacona Park are nearby, for when you need a break from all the charm.

slides.title: Curious about Fernwood?
slides.body: Ask me anything about the neighbourhood. I promise to keep the history lecture short. (Ish.)

caption:
Fernwood, Victoria neighbourhood spotlight 🏡 Close to downtown, full of heritage homes, and home to a church that quit its day job to do theatre 🎭

A few things to know:

🏠 The name comes from Fernwood Manor, the stone villa surveyor Benjamin Pearse built here in 1860 (demolished in 1969)
💧 Before that, the area was Spring Ridge. Its springs were an important source of Victoria's drinking water until the mid-1870s
🚋 Fernwood Square, at Gladstone and Fernwood, was the end of the Spring Ridge streetcar line from 1891 to 1948
🎭 The Belfry Theatre has been in the former Emmanuel Baptist Church (main building 1892) since 1976
🏘️ Many streets and houses date from 1890 to 1912, and the village is a heritage conservation area
🏫 Victoria High School's building went up in 1911–14

Live in Fernwood? Tell me your favourite spot in the comments 👇 (Gatekeeping is allowed. I'll respect it. Mostly.)
